🚨 Wash Sales

                
Disallowed losses for  · cross-broker scan with ±30 day window. HIGH = same-symbol stock buy. MEDIUM = STO put on same underlying (wheel-strategy).

                

                

                

                  About wash sales: The IRS disallows a loss when a "substantially identical" security is acquired within 30 days before or after the loss. Disallowed losses are added to the cost basis of the replacement security (not yet automated in The Forge — v2.3.x+). Selling a put option (CSP) on the same underlying as a stock loss can trigger a wash under IRS rules because it functions like maintaining the position. Option-on-option scan (v2.3.2a): Closing a put or call at a realized loss and selling a new option of the same type on the same underlying within ±30 days is also flagged. Whether two options with different strikes or expiries are "substantially identical" is interpretation-dependent — discuss with your CPA. Only realized losses (negative P&L) are scanned; profitable BTC trades are excluded by design. Disclaimer: This engine is informational, not tax advice — consult a CPA for filing.

🚀 Getting Started

                
The Forge is a single-file investment tracker that runs entirely in your browser. Your data lives in Google Drive — no server, no account required beyond Google OAuth.


                
First-time setup

                
    
                  
  1. 1
    Set a password — chosen on first run, minimum 8 characters. Hashed locally with PBKDF2 (100,000 SHA-256 iterations, per-user random salt). Forge never transmits it. If you forget it, use Forgot Password — your recovery key lives in Drive.
    2. 
                  
  2. 2
    Connect Google Drive — click the Drive status dot (top-right toolbar). OAuth opens in a popup. Once connected, Forge reads and writes forge_data.json to your Drive root.
    3. 
                  
  3. 3
    Import your first CSV — go to Import in the sidebar. Supported: Schwab transaction CSV, Fidelity transaction CSV. Forge categorizes every row, shows a preview, then waits for your commit. See Import & Reconciliation →
    4. 
                  
  4. 4
    Add API keys — go to Settings → API Keys. A free Finnhub key unlocks live VIX, economic calendar, news, and OHLC data throughout the app. See API Keys →
    5. 
                


                
Tab overview

                
📊 DashboardPortfolio summary — 8 hero KPIs, ETF cards, stock cards, stats strip.

                
📈 ETFsYieldMax ETF detail — coverage bars, dividend history, ROC tracking.

                
⚡ OptionsWheel strategy log — P&L, win rate, profit factor, calendar heatmap.

                
🏦 StocksEquity positions — FIFO cost basis, realized/unrealized G/L.

                
🌿 FidelityFidelity account — DCA positions, Roth/taxable breakdown.

                
🔬 Deep DivePer-symbol equity curve, heatmap, trade-level drill-down.

                
📜 TransactionsUnified event log — all brokers, filterable by type, searchable, sortable.

                
💰 TaxesRealized gains summary — short/long-term splits, wash sale flags.

                
📥 ImportCSV importer — Schwab + Fidelity. Reconciliation gate runs at commit.

                
🎯 OS-GuidanceOptions selling decision surface — criteria gate, live market tiles, CSP trade structures.

              


              
              

                
📥 Import & Reconciliation

                
Forge ingests broker CSVs and reconciles your reported cash balance against what it can derive from your transaction history.


                
Import flow

                
    
                  
  1. 1
    Download your transaction history CSV from Schwab or Fidelity. In Schwab: Accounts → History → Export. In Fidelity: Activity & Orders → Download.
    2. 
                  
  2. 2
    Drop the file in the Import tab. Forge parses every row and categorizes it into Stocks, Options, Dividends, or Interest. Unrecognized rows go to a Review Queue.
    3. 
                  
  3. 3
    Review the categorization preview. Deduplication runs automatically — rows already in your data are skipped.
    4. 
                  
  4. 4
    Click Commit. Forge writes the new rows, runs the reconciliation gate, and shows you the drift result.
    5. 
                


                
Understanding drift

                
After commit, Forge compares your reported cash balance (from the CSV) against the derived balance it reconstructs from your transaction history. The gap is called drift.

                

                  
StateDriftMeaning

                  
                    
✓ PERFECT$0.00Reported and derived balances match exactly.

                    
~ SUB-$1< $1.00Rounding or fractional shares. No action needed.

                    
⚠ AMBER$1 – $50Likely a wire, ADR fee, or unclassified event. Resolve via Review Queue or manual adjustment.

                    
✕ RED> $50Significant gap. Check for MoneyLink transfers, missing CSV date range, or special distributions.

                  
                


                
Resolving drift

                
Common causes: MoneyLink / wire transfers · ADR custody fees · special non-dividend distributions · reverse splits logged as "Other" · missing CSV date range.

                
    
                  
  1. A
    Review Queue first — unclassified rows from the CSV are held here. Open Settings → Review Queue, classify each row, and re-save. Correct classifications often close the gap entirely.
    2. 
                  
  2. B
    Manual adjustment — for events Forge will never model (wires, ADR fees). Open Settings → Cash & Reconcile → Manual Adjustments, add a labeled amount. Each adjustment reduces drift by that amount.
    3. 
                  
  3. C
    Re-import a wider date range — if your CSV doesn't cover all history back to your first trade, gaps appear. Re-export from the broker with a broader range and reimport. Deduplication prevents double-counting.
    4. 
                


                
Keep the seed pure. The canonical data in Drive is your source of truth. Never hand-edit forge_data.json directly — always use the Import flow so deduplication and reconciliation run correctly.

              


              
              

                
🧮 FIFO & Lot Engine

                
Forge tracks cost basis using FIFO (First In, First Out) — the IRS default method. Each buy creates an open lot. Each sell consumes the oldest lot(s) first.


                
How lots work

                
Example: You buy 10 NFLX at $96 (Apr 17), then 10 more at $92 (Apr 24). You sell 15 shares. FIFO consumes all 10 from the Apr 17 lot first, then 5 from the Apr 24 lot. The remaining 5 shares carry the Apr 24 cost basis.

                
Open lotA buy with shares not yet fully sold. Contributes to unrealized G/L on the Dashboard.

                
Closed lotA buy fully consumed by one or more sells. Contributes to realized G/L.

                
Partial sellA sell that consumes part of the oldest lot. Remaining shares stay open at the original cost.

                
Orphan rowA sell with no matching buy lot — usually from pre-history trades not in your CSV. Visible in Transactions with an orphan indicator.

                
History floorForge uses a rolling floor (last year or 2026, whichever is later) to avoid stale lot math from very old uncovered history.


                
Options lots

                
Each STO (sell-to-open) creates an open options position. A matching BTC (buy-to-close) or Expired event closes it. Assignment flows back into the stock lot engine at the strike price.


                
Wash sales: If you sell a stock at a loss and rebuy within 30 days, the IRS disallows the loss. Forge flags these in the Dashboard banner and applies the basis adjustment automatically. See Taxes & Wash Sales →

              


              
              

                
💰 Cash Reconciliation

                
The Cash Reconciliation system keeps your reported broker cash balance aligned with what Forge can derive from your imported transaction history. Access it at Settings → Cash & Reconcile.


                
The four drift states

                

                  
BadgeThresholdRecommended action

                  
                    
✓ PERFECTExactly $0Nothing to do.

                    
~ <$1Under $1.00Rounding noise — safe to leave.

                    
⚠ AMBER$1 – $50Add a manual adjustment or classify Review Queue items.

                    
✕ REDOver $50Investigate before trusting Dashboard cash figures.

                  
                


                
Three resolution paths

                
Review QueueUnclassified rows held from the CSV. Classify them in Settings → Review Queue. Correct classification automatically reduces drift on next save.

                
Manual adjustmentFor events Forge will never model (wires, ADR fees, special distributions). Each labeled entry subtracts from the drift calculation.

                
Re-importWiden your CSV date range to cover history Forge hasn't seen. Deduplication prevents double-counting on re-import.


                
Reported balance

                
Forge reads your cash balance from the bottom of your Schwab CSV (the "Transactions Total" row). If your CSV is partial (date-filtered), the reported balance may not match what Forge can derive — this is expected and not a bug.


                
Copy queue for Claude — the clipboard button in Settings → Cash & Reconcile exports a structured summary of your drift, open queue items, and recent adjustments. Paste it into Claude to get a reconciliation diagnosis without sharing raw account data.

              


              
              

                
💵 Taxes & Wash Sales

                
Forge tracks realized gains, flags wash sales, and models your effective tax rate so the Dashboard's after-tax figures stay honest. Configure rates and assumptions in Settings → Taxes.


                
Wash sales

                
The IRS disallows a capital loss if you re-buy the same security (or a "substantially identical" one) within 30 days before or after the loss-taking sell. Forge detects this pattern automatically across your imported history.

                

                  
SurfaceWhere it shows up

                  
                    
Dashboard bannerCount + total disallowed loss across all flagged lots. Click through to see the affected transactions.

                    
Transactions rowEach affected sell shows a 🚨 badge; hover for the disallowed amount.

                    
Realized basis adjustmentThe disallowed loss is added to the cost basis of the replacement buy (IRS rule). The Taxes tab realized-G/L total reflects this automatically.

                  
                

                
Manual override: Forge's detector is mechanical — it doesn't know about retirement-account mirrors, spousal accounts, or "substantially identical" judgement calls. Open Transactions → edit row to flag/unflag wash status manually when you've made a corrective decision.


                
Short-term vs long-term

                
Realized gains split by holding period — short-term (held ≤ 1 year, taxed as ordinary income) and long-term (held > 1 year, capital gains rates). Forge applies your configured rates to estimate after-tax proceeds throughout the Dashboard and Taxes tab.


                
Tax Bracket Calculator

                
A sub-tab under Settings → Taxes that estimates your marginal and effective rates from real income inputs.

                
Auto-rowsThree pre-populated income sources: W-2 (paste from your last paystub or W-2), K-1 (LLC distributions), Forge (YTD short-term realized gains, auto-filled from imported data).

                
Marginal bracketsUses the current Federal bracket schedule. Filing status (Single / MFJ / HoH) selectable.

                
GA flat rateGeorgia state income tax modeled as a flat rate. Non-GA states default to GA's value — edit manually if you live elsewhere.

                
Apply to Manual RatesOnce the calculator shows your blended marginal rate, click Apply to write it into the Manual Rates fields used by all Dashboard after-tax displays — no double-entry.


                
SE tax checkbox

                
Self-Employment tax (IRC § 1401) applies if Forge income is treated as dealer rather than investor activity — generally requires active operator status and substantial activity. Toggle the SE checkbox per income row.

                
Effective rate is usually small. SE tax is 15.3% on the first ~$168K (the SS wage base), then 2.9% above. If your W-2 already maxes the SS wage base, only the 2.9% Medicare portion applies to LLC income — effective ~2.7–3.5%. The 3.8% Net Investment Income surtax (above MAGI threshold) is a separate checkbox.


                
Forge is not tax advice. Dealer-vs-investor classification, wash-sale gray areas, and state-specific rules require a CPA. Forge's numbers are estimates designed to inform your tax conversations — not replace them.

              


              
              

                
🎯 OS-Guidance

                
OS-Guidance (Options Selling Guidance) is a live decision surface for cash-secured put (CSP) trading. It answers two questions: Should I enter a trade today? and If yes, what structure?


                
How to use it

                
    
                  
  1. 1
    Pick a symbol from the watchlist pill row (SPY, PLTR, NVDA, NAIL, or any held position). Forge fetches live price, OHLC, VIX, and news.
    2. 
                  
  2. 2
    Pick a timeframe — 0DTE, EOD, 7DTE, 14-21DTE, or 30DTE. Each has different VIX and session thresholds.
    3. 
                  
  3. 3
    Read the Criteria Gate — all rows green = trade is clear. Any red row = specific reason to pause. Manual rows (⚠) require your confirmation (e.g. P/C ratio from Barchart).
    4. 
                  
  4. 4
    Read the Trade Structures — three tiers (Conservative 0.05Δ, Moderate 0.10Δ, Aggressive 0.20Δ) with estimated strike, premium, and credit shown.
    5. 
                  
  5. 5
    Check News & Sentiment — the sentiment banner gives a sizing hint (normal / reduce 30–50% / trade as-is). The gate decides IF. News modifies SIZE.
    6.

P/C ratio — click the ⚠ ↗ enter badge in the criteria gate to open the inline popup. Forge links directly to the correct Barchart page for the active symbol. Enter the ratio, click Confirm. The value is symbol-scoped and resets at midnight ET.


                
News & sentiment

                
The sentiment banner above the trade structures gives a sizing hint based on news flow. Verdict (BULLISH / BEARISH / NEUTRAL) drives the modifier badge (Tailwind / Headwind / Mixed).

                

                  
SourceWhat it provides

                  
                    
Finnhub real sentimentStocks only — pulls bullish%/bearish% + sector average from /news-sentiment. Drives the banner verdict when bull/bear delta ≥ 15pp. Shows "via Finnhub" pill.

                    
Keyword fallbackUsed when Finnhub is unreachable, no key configured, or coverage thin. Classifies headline keywords to BULLISH/BEARISH/NEUTRAL. Shows "keyword" pill.

                    
Per-article pillsAlways keyword-based — Finnhub doesn't expose per-article scores. Color-coded on each news card.

                    
Source denylist14-source blocklist suppresses low-signal aggregator content from both headlines and sentiment input.

                  
                

                
Income-only ETFs (TSLY · ULTY · AMDY · CONY) skip the Finnhub sentiment call — these tickers don't generate meaningful sentiment data. Banner reverts to keyword fallback on these. Cache TTL is 15 min across all news/sentiment paths.

              


              
              

                
🔄 Auto-Roll Alerts

                
Auto-Roll watches your open option positions and flags ones approaching a roll/close decision. It doesn't act — you decide. Alerts surface in two places: the Options tab strip (all positions across brokers) and OS-Guidance row 2.5 (active symbol only).


                
The three triggers

                

                  
TriggerRulePriority

                  
                    
Assignment risk|price − strike| / strike ≤ 2% — strike is within 2% of current spot.High · red

                    
21 DTEDTE ≤ 21 — time-decay window opens.Medium · gold

                    
80% profit(stoAmt − currentMTM) / stoAmt ≥ 0.80 — lock in profits early.Medium · gold

                  
                


                
Triggers stack. A single position can fire multiple triggers at once — all pills show. The row border tint follows the highest priority (red > gold).


                
Dismiss behavior

                
Dismissing an alert is session-only by design. Reload re-fires all active alerts. Reason: time-decaying instruments get more urgent each day, never less — a persistent dismiss could silently hide a position becoming MORE urgent.

                
Position closedDrops out of alerts naturally — no manual cleanup needed.

                
Rolled to new expiryA new tradeId enters the lot engine; a fresh alert fires if any trigger re-evaluates true.


                
80% profit trigger needs Live Prices. The mark-to-market math relies on cached option marks populated by the Dashboard Live Prices button. Habit: click Live Prices on app entry to keep marks fresh through the session. Without recent marks, the 80%-profit check silently skips that position — the other two triggers still fire.

              


              
              

                
📜 Roll Ledger

                
The Rolls 🔄 tab in the Options view is a win/loss scorecard for rolled positions. When you roll — buy-to-close one leg and sell-to-open another on the same day, confirmed in the import picker — Forge links the legs into a chain. Roll the same position again and the new leg joins the same chain, so a multi-roll defense shows as one row, oldest leg → newest.


                
Why a separate scorecard? A credit roll always feels like a win — cash comes in — but serially rolling a loser down-and-out for small credits is just financing a bad position with new premium. The ledger keeps the honest numbers apart so that pattern can't hide.


                
The three numbers — kept rigorously separate

                

                  
ColumnWhat it is

                  
                    
BankedRealized P&L of the chain's closed legs. Tax-true — the same number in Closed and Taxes. This is the only figure that's real money so far.

                    
Roll creditNet cash collected at each roll event. A behavioral diagnostic, not profit — it double-counts intermediate premium against Banked, so it is shown in neutral grey and never summed into any total.

                    
Unrealized / Mark→nowThe live leg's mark-to-market (from Live Prices) and Banked + that unrealized. Shows "—" until marks are fetched, or when the provider lists no quote for that strike/expiry (common on thinly-traded strikes) — then the premium-collected basis stands.

                    
If worthlessChain total if the open leg expires worthless (keeps full premium). The break-even read: the open leg must keep at least the banked loss for the chain to come out even.

                    
WashHow much of the banked loss is wash-disallowed (gold). A subset of Banked, not a separate line — it flags tax deferred into the replacement leg's basis. Reads the Wash Sales engine; see Taxes & Wash Sales →

                  
                


                
Terminal verdict

                
A chain only earns a win/loss verdict once it has ended — an open chain reads ● Live (pending), never a win just for collecting a credit.

                
● LiveLast leg still open — no verdict yet.

                
✓ Win / ✗ LossChain closed (expired worthless, or bought-to-close not rolled) — by the sign of total realized.

                
⇒ AssignedIts own bucket, not win/loss — on the wheel, assignment means you took the shares; the premium reduced your basis.


                
Header scorecard

                
Chains, win rate (over terminated, non-assigned chains only), average rolls per chain, total banked across all chains, and — when any chain carries a wash — a Wash-deferred tile.


                
Display only. The ledger reads the stored roll links and computes nothing that touches your accounting — it moves no realized or tax number. Rolls also surface on the open-position card (🔄 badge) and in Deep Dive's "How Options Closed" (the count of BTC closes that were rolls).

              


              
              

                
🔑 API Keys

                
Forge talks to two external services. Finnhub needs a free API key. Yahoo Finance needs no key but does need a CORS path — either your own Cloudflare Worker (recommended; required for options chains and intraday VWAP) or the public corsproxy.io fallback (VIX and /quote only).


                
Getting a Finnhub key

                
    
                  
  1. 1
    Go to finnhub.io and sign up for a free account. No credit card required.
    2. 
                  
  2. 2
    Copy your API key from the Finnhub dashboard.
    3. 
                  
  3. 3
    In Forge: Settings → API Keys → Finnhub API Key. Paste and save.
    4. 
                


                
Setting up the Forge Proxy (Cloudflare Worker)

                
Yahoo Finance options chains and 1-minute intraday endpoints require a server-side "crumb" auth dance that corsproxy.io can't replicate. The Forge Proxy is a small Cloudflare Worker you deploy in your own account that handles this for you. Cloudflare's free tier covers Forge's traffic with substantial headroom.

                
    
                  
  1. 1
    Sign up at dash.cloudflare.com (free) and navigate to Workers & Pages → Create Worker.
    2. 
                  
  2. 2
    Replace the default worker code with the Forge Proxy source (the project's worker.js — implements crumb fetch, origin allowlist, and five endpoint paths: /quote, /options, /intraday, /vix, /econ-calendar).
    3. 
                  
  3. 3
    In the worker source, set ALLOWED_ORIGIN to the URL where you load Forge. This origin-gates the Worker so only your Forge instance can call it — any other origin gets a 403.
    4. 
                  
  4. 4
    Click Deploy. Cloudflare assigns a URL like forge-proxy.you.workers.dev.
    5. 
                  
  5. 5
    In Forge: Settings → API Keys → Forge Proxy URL. Paste the URL, save, then click Test Proxy. A green ✓ confirms the round-trip; red shows the failure mode in the diagnostic line.
    6. 
                

                
Without the Worker, Forge falls back to corsproxy.io for simple Yahoo endpoints (VIX, /quote). Options-chain and intraday VWAP criteria will show "Worker required" and skip in the gate. The fetch failure modal explains this in real time when a call fails — see Security model →


                
What each source unlocks

                

                  
FeatureSourceWithout it

                  
                    
Price, RSI, ATR, ADX, TRENDYahoo (corsproxy or Worker)Always available — corsproxy fallback works

                    
VIX liveYahoo (corsproxy or Worker)OS-Guidance shows "awaiting data"

                    
Ex-div / earnings datesYahoo (corsproxy or Worker)Always available

                    
Yahoo company namesYahoo (corsproxy or Worker)Falls back to broker label / static map

                    
Options chain (CSP structures)Yahoo via Worker onlyTrade structure tiles stay empty

                    
Intraday VWAP (EOD criterion)Yahoo via Worker onlyVWAP 3hr+ criterion skips

                    
FOMC / CPI / NFP auto-checkFinnhubCriterion shows as manual

                    
News & real sentimentFinnhubBanner uses keyword fallback

                    
OHLC + IV Rank + PQ tilesFinnhubTiles remain in loading state

                    
Split detection (14-day)Finnhub (via OHLC)Split criterion shows manual

                  
                


                
Cache TTLs. Forge caches every external fetch to stay well within free-tier rate limits: VIX 5 min · OHLC 1 hr · news/sentiment 15 min · econ calendar 30 min · options chain 5 min · intraday VWAP 5 min · Yahoo company names 30 days.


                
Adding a new API in the future? The Forge HTML ships with a Content-Security-Policy <meta> tag near the top of the file that allowlists every connect-src host explicitly. When you wire a new external integration: (1) add the host to the connect-src directive in the meta tag, and (2) update the labeled comment block immediately above it so future-you knows why the host is there. Both changes live together — don't update one without the other or you'll spend 20 minutes debugging a CSP error that should have been a 30-second fix.

              


              
              

                
🔒 Data & Privacy

                
Forge is a zero-server app. Your financial data never leaves your browser session except to your own Google Drive.


                
Where your data lives

                
Google DriveAll persistent data is stored in forge_data.json in your Drive root. Only your Google account can access it.

                
sessionStorageYour session token (password hash) is cached here for the duration of your browser session. Cleared on tab close.

                
localStorageStores your password hash (PBKDF2) and auto-logout timer preference only. No financial data is ever written here.

                
Yahoo name cacheStored in appData.stockNames (Drive-persisted, 30-day TTL). Maps tickers to longName/shortName so cards show "Palantir Technologies" instead of broker labels. Fire-and-forget refresh after each Stocks render.

                
No serverForge has no backend. The HTML file itself is the entire app. API calls go directly from your browser to Yahoo Finance and Finnhub.


                
Pre-save backups

                
Before every save to Drive, Forge writes a timestamped backup file (default: last 5 days retained). If a save goes wrong, your previous data is recoverable from Drive. Manage backup retention in Settings → Data Management.


                
Security model

                
Forge's threat model assumes the HTML file may run on a host you don't fully control. Five layers defend against credential theft, prompt-injection from data sources, and accidental data leaks.

                
PBKDF2 passwordYour password (min 8 chars) is hashed with PBKDF2-SHA256 at 100,000 iterations using a per-user random 16-byte salt. Only the derived hash ever lives in localStorage in the format pbkdf2$<iter>$<salt>$<hash>. Forge cannot recover the plaintext — Forgot Password flows through Drive OAuth recovery instead.

                
CSP allowlistA Content-Security-Policy meta tag explicitly allowlists every host Forge can talk to (Google APIs, Yahoo Finance via Worker/corsproxy, Finnhub, your Worker URL). All other connect-src targets are blocked at the browser level — even an injected script can't exfiltrate data, the browser refuses the request.

                
Fetch failure modalWhen external calls fail in bursts, Forge surfaces a single modal with full diagnostics rather than spamming toasts. Falling back to corsproxy.io requires explicit consent (in-memory only — resets on reload). The "Disable fallback · resume Worker routing" button reverts that consent mid-session without reloading.

                
Login lockoutAfter 10 failed password attempts in a row, the password path locks out and forces recovery via Drive OAuth. Counter clears on successful login or password reset. Resists brute-force attacks against the localStorage hash.

                
XSS escapesAll free-form fields from external sources (CSV descriptions, news headlines, ticker names, news URLs) pass through HTML-escape helpers before rendering. URLs additionally enforce ^https?:// — javascript:/data:/vbscript: hrefs are stripped.


                
Exporting your data

                
Raw JSONDownload forge_data.json directly from Google Drive at any time — it is human-readable.

                
Transactions CSVUse the Transactions tab filter + sort to narrow the view. CSV export is a future backlog item.


                
Sharing with Claude: The "Copy queue for Claude" button in Cash Reconciliation is the intended way to share Forge data for analysis. Never paste your full forge_data.json into a public chat — it contains your complete trade history and cost basis.
